lesson.title: The Centre Is Not the Plan
lesson.hook: You recover to the centre—and still get caught covering the wrong court.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you recover, name the likely reply before choosing the spot.

pro.label: Why Djokovic gets there
pro.moment: Holger Rune on Djokovic: "He's reading the game extremely well, better than anyone, I think." Greg Rusedski calls efficiency of movement the key.
pro.read: Recovery starts with reading their reply.

drill.name: Call the reply
drill.how: After each of your shots, call out where their reply is most likely to go, before they hit it, and recover toward that. Your partner counts your correct calls.

steps.name: Deep and wide
steps.sit: Your deep crosscourt pushes them outside the sideline. You finish balanced.
opts: Left of centre, behind the line
Right of centre, behind the line
steps.payoff: Shade toward the angle your shot gave them.
steps.principle: Your shot changed where they can hit, so the middle moved too.
steps.why: From outside the sideline, their safest reply is crosscourt, back to your right. Shading right covers it; dead centre leaves you stretching.
steps.take: Your shot moved their angles — shade right, stay behind the line.

lines.A: Their crosscourt angle runs away from you — too far to get there.
lines.B: You gave them the line — too far to get there.
lines.C: Dead centre, their angle stretches you — you only just reach it.
lines.D: Shaded right, you're in time for their best reply.

steps.name: Shorter ball, you recovering
steps.sit: Your shorter ball leaves them balanced, and you're still getting back.
steps.q: Where do you recover to now?
opts: Move in and take time away
steps.payoff: Get nearer the centre and give yourself time.
steps.principle: When they're balanced and you're not, time matters more than the angle.
steps.why: A balanced opponent can go either way, and you're late already. A step deeper near the centre buys the time to cover both.
steps.take: Short ball and you're off balance? Recover deeper, nearer centre.

lines.A: They go to the open side — too far to get there.
lines.B: Moving in, you run out of time — their deep ball is past you.
lines.C: Deeper and central, you reach it — stretched, but still in it.
lines.D: Staying wide leaves the whole line — too far to get there.

steps.name: Four line replies
steps.sit: Same deep ball. They've gone down the line the last four times.
steps.q: What should those four replies change?
opts: Shade far left to cover the line
Charge in to cut it off
steps.payoff: Respect the pattern with one step, not a guess.
steps.principle: Your shot sets the default. What they keep doing can nudge it.
steps.why: Four line replies are worth a step, not the whole crosscourt. One step over covers both; a big move guesses and leaves the other side open.
steps.take: Four line replies earn one step toward the line — not a guess.

lines.A: One step over covers both replies — you're in time.
lines.B: They go line again — you only just get there.
lines.C: Too far left — their crosscourt gets past you.
lines.D: Charging in, you only just get back to their deep reply.
